title: Co-creating the future of fashion with Google
gist: Google's Envisioning Studio built two custom Google Flow tools with fashion designers Jane Wade and Sergio Hudson for New York Fashion Week, targeting the operational bottlenecks (casting, fittings, re-rendering) that eat designers' time rather than the creative act itself, and is opening Google Flow up as a no-code, natural-language tool-builder.

themes.theme: AI targets fashion's operational bottlenecks, not the creative act

insights.claim: Independent fashion designers spend most of their time on administrative tasks, factory logistics, and vendor coordination rather than actually designing clothes, according to Google's framing of where the real friction lies in the fashion production process.
insights.speaker: Yeawon Choi
insights.so_what: Signals where AI creative tools may capture value in fashion and similar creative industries: automating operational overhead, not replacing the core creative decisions.
insights.quote: Administrative tasks, factory logistics, and vendor coordination take up the bulk of their days, leaving very little time for design.
insights.locator: Ask an independent fashion designer how they actually spend their time

insights.claim: In-person casting and fittings typically consume up to three full days for a design team; the custom Google Flow tool Styling Suite let designer Jane Wade curate hair, makeup, accessories, shoes, and garments on digital models and balance looks virtually before cutting or sewing physical samples.
insights.speaker: Yeawon Choi
insights.so_what: Quantifies a concrete time and physical-material savings case for generative AI in apparel production workflows, useful for benchmarking AI ROI claims in fashion.
insights.quote: In-person casting and fittings typically consume up to three full days for a design team.

insights.claim: Previously, each revision to a runway's lighting or props required commissioning a new 3D rendering, adding cost every time; the custom Google Flow tool Runway Visualization let designer Sergio Hudson simulate and adjust his venue's lighting, props, and model paths live within a fixed budget, eliminating that back-and-forth.
insights.speaker: Yeawon Choi
insights.so_what: Shows generative simulation tools removing a recurring, per-revision cost bottleneck (re-rendering) in physical production planning, a pattern likely repeatable in other set-design or event industries.
insights.locator: Grounding runway design in a real budget

insights.claim: Despite general excitement about AI in the fashion industry, many AI-in-fashion projects remain stuck in theoretical testing rather than reaching actual production use, which is the gap this Google Flow collaboration is positioned as bridging.
insights.speaker: Yeawon Choi
insights.so_what: Useful skepticism check for evaluating AI-in-creative-industry adoption claims generally: look for evidence of tools reaching real production runways, not just demos or pilots.
insights.quote: many projects remain stuck in theoretical testing
insights.locator: Moving fashion AI out of pilot mode

themes.theme: Google Flow as a no-code tool-building platform

insights.claim: Google Flow now lets users build their own custom design tools by describing the desired tool or workflow in natural language, with no coding required, extending Flow beyond a generative media tool into a general-purpose AI tool-builder.
insights.speaker: Yeawon Choi
insights.so_what: Signals Google's direction for Flow: a platform for building bespoke workflow tools per vertical, which could compete with niche vertical SaaS (e.g. fashion production software) if it generalizes beyond this case.
insights.locator: Build your own bespoke tools in Google Flow
